gotchas: Use /buy (signed out, plan buttons are links, e.g. a[aria-label="Buy now: Plus"]). /plans renders them as buttons behind a cookie banner in an iframe (press Enter on Decline inside iframe[src*="consent"]).

The checkout page (/checkout) opens a "Log in or sign up" dialog over it. Its email field submits on Enter. Do not target button:has-text("Continue") — it also matches "Continue with Apple"/Microsoft and opens a third-party popup. Email then password, each submitted with Enter.
Signing in from a new browser sent a one-time code (input[autocomplete=one-time-code]); that is the account owner's handoff. Purchase needs the account.

Card fields are in Dropbox's own iframe (iframe[name="cc_iframe"], cf.dropboxpayments.com) as plain autocomplete inputs (cc-number, cc-exp MM/YY, cc-csc); Country and Billing ZIP are on the page under it. Credit card is the default radio; PayPal is the alternative. A dropboxcaptcha.com frame is present.

Verified 2026-10-06 through the proxy (US tunnel) with the public test card under a verification-only key: the cc_iframe fields filled with no error (filled while the login dialog was still open; the code step was not completed). Stopped before Purchase.

Observed 2026-10-07 (proxy, US tunnel): signing in first at dropbox.com/login (email + Enter, password + Enter) asked for no code this time. Signed in, /buy shows no "Buy now: Plus" control; open /plans and click the first visible a:has-text("Buy now"). The checkout then has Postal Code on the page (role=textbox name Postal Code) and the same cc_iframe; the public test card filled with no error while signed in. A signed-out /checkout may show the card form with no login dialog until Purchase.
